channel.title: The Garden Island - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Garden Island (thegardenisland.com)

item.title: EDITORIAL: Put ban-LNG bill on back burner
item.description: Hawaii’s people need more clarity about what’s ahead on the road toward the state’s clean-energy goals. That means a big public conversation about liquefied natural gas (LNG) must happen before it’s time for top decision-makers to change tacks again.

item.title: Night work continues for the Kuhio Highway Waterline Project
item.description: LIHUE — Night work with one-lane closures will continue in the Lihue area through all of February, weekdays from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., weather permitting, for the Kuhio Highway (Hardy-Oxford) Waterline Project, announced the Department of Water (DOW) and its contractor Alpha Inc.

item.title: Happy Camper for Saturday, February 7, 2026
item.description: If everything goes smoothly, Kapaa High School boys soccer and the Waimea High School girls basketball teams should be involved in the Hawaii High School Athletic Association Division II state championships of their respective athletic competitions today at arenas located on Hawaii Island for the girls basketball and on Oahu for the boys soccer.

item.title: Somers Scholarship available for West Kauai women
item.description: LIHUE — The PEO Chapter L-Hawaii of Lihue announced that a $2,000 scholarship in memory of Lois Robinson Somers and Lawrence Hutchinson Somers is currently available. Application forms are available at the chapter’s website at www.peokauai.org under the Somers Scholarship tab.

item.title: Cleanup continues after mess left by Kilauea’s recent episode
item.description: A week-and-a-half after Episode 41 of Kilauea’s yearlong summit eruption deposited tephra — lightweight volcanic glass debris — over a sizable area surrounding Halemaumau Crater, residents of Volcano are still digging out.

item.title: OED announces recipients of County of Kauai cultural grants
item.description: LIHUE — The County of Kauai Office of Economic Development (OED) is pleased to announce the recipients of its Fiscal Year 2025-26 Kauai Cultural Program and Events Grants.

item.title: Officials warn of potentially inclement weather into next week
item.description: LIHUE — County of Kauai officials are urging the public to be vigilant due to potential severe weather conditions beginning this weekend and continuing into next week.

item.title: Waimea girls advance at the Division II state girls basketball championships
item.description: HILO — Waimea High School, seeded No. 2 in the Division II state girls basketball championships, beat unseeded Mid Pacific Institute, 52-39, on Thursday to advance to the semifinals today at the Hilo Civic Center on Hawaii Island.

item.title: Hawaii legislative bills advance to unmask ICE agents
item.description: The first of several Hawaii legislative bills that would unmask federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents was met with concerns Tuesday from the Honolulu Police Department and state Department of Law Enforcement that backup officers from their departments also could be identified while supporting local undercover operations.

item.title: SBA programs for native businesses face scrutiny
item.description: The Native Hawaiian Organizations Association is urging President Donald Trump’s administration to distinguish between “isolated allegations” about the Small Business Administration’s program aimed at developing native-run businesses and its success expanding economic opportunity, as U.S. Rep. Ed Case calls for a formal review.
